name: Bar Preacher Curl
variant: Preacher-bench curl with a curl bar or straight bar, upper arms supported on the angled pad; dumbbell, cable, and machine preacher curls are separate variants if precision is needed.
description: Sit or stand at the preacher bench with the upper arms supported on the pad, take a comfortable supinated or semi-supinated bar grip, curl without lifting the upper arms off the pad, then lower under control until the elbows are nearly long without collapsing into the bottom position.

hypertrophy.rationale: Strong focused elbow-flexor accessory with upper-arm support and direct preacher-curl training evidence, though the short-length loading profile limits it versus long-length curl variants.

strength.rationale: Useful for local elbow-flexion strength, but external support and single-joint loading make it a poor global strength anchor.

joint_resilience.rationale: Controlled elbow loading can be useful, but the supported bottom position can be unforgiving if range and load are pushed aggressively.

athletic_transfer.rationale: Almost no direct sport or whole-body transfer beyond elbow-flexor capacity.

control.rationale: The bench removes most postural and shoulder-control demand.

fatigue_efficiency.rationale: Very focused local arm stimulus with little systemic fatigue.

setup.rationale: Requires a preacher bench plus suitable bar, and pad geometry can vary between gyms.

ease.rationale: Simple path once positioned, though the user must avoid bouncing or overextending at the bottom.

progression.rationale: Load and reps are trackable, especially with plate-loaded bars, but bar jumps and bench geometry can affect repeatability.

support.rationale: The preacher pad supports the upper arm and constrains shoulder movement.

primary.name: Biceps brachii
primary.evidenceShort: Preacher curl evidence directly targets and measures the biceps brachii.
primary.evidence: Dumbbell preacher curl EMG measured biceps brachii, and barbell preacher-curl training evidence supports biceps brachii hypertrophy from preacher-pattern loading. The supported upper-arm position makes biceps brachii the intended visible primary target.

secondary.name: Brachialis
secondary.evidenceShort: Preacher curl training evidence includes elbow-flexor thickness beyond biceps alone.
secondary.evidence: Recent preacher-versus-Bayesian curl training evidence assessed biceps brachii and brachialis thickness adaptations, supporting brachialis inclusion as a secondary elbow-flexor target. It is not listed as primary because the visible target and direct EMG record are strongest for biceps brachii.

secondary.name: Brachioradialis
secondary.evidenceShort: Curl handgrip EMG supports brachioradialis as an elbow-flexor contributor.
secondary.evidence: Bar and handgrip curl EMG measured brachioradialis activity during curl variants. It is secondary here because a supported supinated or semi-supinated preacher curl is programmed mainly for biceps brachii.

support.name: Wrist flexors
support.evidenceShort: Grip and wrist posture require forearm support.
support.evidence: Forearm EMG evidence supports wrist flexor involvement in grip and wrist-position control. They are shown as support because the bar must be held stable through the curl.

evidence.verdict: Bar preacher curl: biceps brachii primary; brachialis and brachioradialis secondary; wrist flexors support.
evidence.clinicalShort: Preacher-curl evidence supports the biceps target; bar shape, pad angle, and lower-end range can meaningfully change stress.
evidence.limitsShort: Pad angle, shoulder position, bar shape, grip width, bottom range, elbow comfort, load, and tempo can change stimulus and tolerance.
evidence.summary: The bar preacher curl is classified as a supported elbow-flexion accessory. Direct preacher-curl EMG and training evidence supports biceps brachii as the primary visible target. Brachialis and brachioradialis are visible secondary contributors based on preacher training data, curl handgrip EMG, and elbow-flexor mechanics. Wrist flexors are listed only for grip and wrist stabilization.
evidence.clinicalInterpretation: This movement is useful when the user wants a constrained arm accessory with less torso and shoulder movement than a standing curl. It should not be collapsed with incline, standing, cable, dumbbell preacher, machine preacher, hammer, or reverse curl entries once the app needs finer variant control.
evidence.limitations: This MVP entry groups straight bar and EZ/curl-bar preacher curls. If wrist comfort, grip angle, or bar mechanics become central, straight-bar and EZ-bar preacher curls should split. Dumbbell preacher EMG and barbell preacher training evidence are close but not identical to every commercial curl-bar preacher setup.

studies.finding: Compared biceps brachii EMG across incline dumbbell curl, standing dumbbell curl, and preacher curl conditions.
studies.citation: Oliveira LF, Matta TT, Alves DS, Garcia MAC, Vieira TMM. Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls. Journal of Sports Science and Medicine. 2009;8(1):24-29.
studies.relevance: Direct preacher-curl shoulder-position evidence for biceps brachii activity.

studies.finding: Compared cable and barbell preacher curl training performed at different muscle-length emphases and measured elbow-flexor strength and hypertrophy adaptations.
studies.citation: Nunes JP, Jacinto JL, Ribeiro AS, Mayhew JL, Nakamura M, Capel DM, Santos LR, Aguiar AF. Placing Greater Torque at Shorter or Longer Muscle Lengths? Effects of Cable vs. Barbell Preacher Curl Training on Muscular Strength and Hypertrophy in Young Adults. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 2020;17(16):5859. doi:10.3390/ijerph17165859.
studies.relevance: Direct barbell preacher curl training evidence for elbow-flexor strength and hypertrophy scoring.

studies.type: Preacher versus Bayesian curl training study
studies.shortCitation: Attarieh et al., Eur J Sport Sci, 2025
studies.finding: Compared shoulder-flexed preacher curl and shoulder-extended Bayesian cable curl training for biceps brachii and brachialis thickness and strength outcomes.
studies.citation: Attarieh M, Jo E, Ribeiro AS, et al. Comparison Between Shoulder Flexed and Extended Positions During Cable Biceps Curls for Biceps Brachii and Brachialis Muscle Growth and Elbow Flexor Strength. European Journal of Sport Science. 2025.
studies.relevance: Close preacher-pattern evidence for biceps brachii and brachialis adaptation and shoulder-position boundaries.

studies.finding: Straight barbell, EZ-bar, and dumbbell curls produced different biceps brachii and brachioradialis EMG patterns across repetition phases.
studies.citation: Marcolin G, Panizzolo FA, Petrone N, Moro T, Grigoletto D, Piccolo D, Paoli A. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ. 2018;6:e5165. doi:10.7717/peerj.5165.
studies.relevance: Bar-curl evidence for brachioradialis involvement and bar-variant boundaries.

studies.finding: Supinated, pronated, and neutral cable curl handgrips changed biceps brachii, brachioradialis, and anterior deltoid excitation in competitive bodybuilders.
studies.citation: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Toninelli N, Padovan R, Esposito F, Ce E. Biceps Brachii and Brachioradialis Excitation in Biceps Curl Exercise: Different Handgrips, Different Synergy. Sports. 2023;11(3):64. doi:10.3390/sports11030064.
studies.relevance: Handgrip-specific curl evidence for brachioradialis contribution and variant limits.

studies.type: Forearm rotation and wrist muscle EMG
studies.shortCitation: Ikeda et al., J Orthop Surg Res, 2025
studies.finding: Wrist flexor and extensor activity changed with forearm rotation during controlled wrist torque tasks.
studies.citation: Ikeda K, Kaneoka K, Matsunaga N, Ikumi A, Yamazaki M, Yoshii Y. Effects of forearm rotation on wrist flexor and extensor muscle activities. Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research. 2025;20(1):53. doi:10.1186/s13018-024-05363-x.
studies.relevance: Forearm and wrist-position evidence for grip and wrist support.

studies.type: Forearm EMG during wrist and finger movements
studies.finding: Multi-channel EMG quantified forearm muscle activity during wrist and finger movement tasks.
studies.citation: Gazzoni M, Celadon N, Mastrapasqua D, Paleari M, Margaria V, Ariano P. Quantifying forearm muscle activity during wrist and finger movements by means of multi-channel electromyography. PLoS ONE. 2014;9(10):e109943. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0109943.
studies.relevance: Broader forearm EMG context for gripping and wrist-position stabilization.
